title: Walthamstow
intro: A creative town with William Morris's family home, a medieval village, one of London's longest street markets and a huge wetland nature reserve.

items.name: William Morris Gallery and Lloyd Park
items.blurb: The Georgian house where William Morris lived as a young man, now a free gallery of his work, with Lloyd Park and its moat behind it.
items.tip: Free entry; the tea room looks onto the park.

items.name: Walthamstow Wetlands
items.blurb: Working reservoirs opened to the public as a nature reserve in 2017, with miles of paths, birdlife and an old engine house turned into a visitor centre and café.
items.tip: Free; climb the Coppermill Tower when it is open for the view.

items.name: God's Own Junkyard
items.blurb: A warehouse packed with glowing neon signs and film props, with a café inside.
items.tip: Open weekends; free to wander in.

items.name: Walthamstow Stadium
items.blurb: The Art Deco frontage of the old greyhound stadium, with its famous neon sign, kept and listed when the track closed and the site became homes.
items.tip: Best seen after dark when the neon is lit.

items.name: Walthamstow Village
items.blurb: The old village around St Mary's church, with the 18th-century Vestry House Museum, the timber-framed Ancient House and cafés on Orford Road.
items.tip: Visit on a Sunday for the farmers' market on Orford Road.

items.name: Walthamstow Marshes
items.blurb: Wild grazing marsh in the Lea Valley beside the River Lea, with towpath walks south to Hackney and Springfield Park.
items.tip: Follow the towpath to Springfield Park for coffee by the river.
